basis: Intestinal fructose malabsorption defines this condition; unlike hereditary fructose intolerance, it does not imply systemic metabolic injury.
Invasive Aspergillus infection causes pulmonary pneumonia and nodules; extrapulmonary dissemination is not universal or established here at >=30%.
Corynebacterial infection directly causes chronic skin ulceration; systemic toxin complications are uncommon in cutaneous disease.
Postencephalitic substantia nigra degeneration causes parkinsonism; prior infection does not establish ongoing infectious or immune-mediated disease.
Bone fragility defines OI; dentinogenesis imperfecta reported in 1/1. Pulmonary damage frequency is uncertain; respiratory restriction may be skeletal. Stones are separate.
Bacterial infection directly inflames the conjunctiva.
Myoclonic epilepsy is a neurologic seizure disorder; no additional organ damage is established.
Congenital skeletal myopathy; ophthalmoplegia in 2/5 and ptosis in 2/2 support ocular dysfunction. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle weakness.
Viral infection umbrella; organ tropism varies substantially among subtypes, with no additional damaged organ established across most patients.
Heritable pulmonary arterial hypertension directly affects pulmonary vessels; dyspnea does not establish lung parenchymal damage.
Syndromic intellectual disability establishes neurodevelopmental involvement; no additional organ phenotype is supplied.
RD3-related congenital retinal dystrophy causes severe visual loss or blindness.
Cutaneous disease predominates across symptomatic cases; visceral and mucosal HPO findings reflect distinct subtypes and should not be generalized across the umbrella.
The cavernous vascular lesion is located in the retina; no systemic vascular involvement is established.
Congenital glaucoma causes ocular hypertension, corneal changes and optic disc damage.
The definition specifies nonsyndromic intellectual disability; carbohydrate transport ancestry does not establish metabolic disease across this umbrella.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and cerebellar hypoplasia define disease; ankle contractures in 5/5 support skeletal involvement. Visual impairment is predominantly cerebral.
Craniofacial dysostosis, bilateral hearing loss and microcephaly with learning disability characterize the syndrome; cardiac lesions occur in only 5-29%.
Deficiency of essential nutrients or calories defines the disorder; specific blood, bone, eye and other injuries depend on the deficient nutrient.
Meier-Gorlin skeletal growth abnormalities and microtia define the syndrome; renal hypoplasia reported in 1/1, although subtype evidence is limited.
The defining triad comprises cardiomyopathy, hormonal gonadal dysfunction and cutaneous collagenomas.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability are common defining manifestations; other organ abnormalities vary with deletion extent.
Skeletal dysplasia defines disease; cataract/microphthalmia, callosal agenesis and VSD each occur in 30-79%. Omphalocele, also 30-79%, omitted at cap.
Motor neuron degeneration causes progressive muscle atrophy and near-universal diaphragm denervation/paralysis (11/11); respiratory failure is neuromuscular.
Developmental abnormality of the iris and anterior chamber angle; systemic manifestations are restricted to particular subtypes.
